label: FP
reason: Both alerts are False Positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) claims user input reaches an HTML response sink, but the switch statement in doSomething assigns a constant "bob" to bar when switchTarget is 'B', blocking user input. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection) claims user input reaches the SQL query sink, but the same switch statement ensures bar is "bob", making the SQL query safe. Neither sink receives attacker-controlled data.

evidence.note: Switch statement logic: switchTarget is 'B', causing bar to be assigned constant "bob" instead of param.
SQL query construction uses bar, which resolves to constant "bob" on this path.
Response print location for Alert 1; content derives from safe bar constant.
